top.headline: Nasdaq 100 dips into bear territory intraday, recovers to close at 26,047
top.why: The index touched -20% from its record before a thin-volume rebound; Friday's half session is the next test.
points: Intraday low 24,970.66 on 25 Nov, 20.03% below the 6 Oct record close of 31,224.47; closed 26,046.90 (-0.64%)
Triggers: hot core PCE, tariff proposals, Micron -10%, Nvidia and AMD about -8% early, S&P CreditWatch negative on Nvidia
Closing basis it is a correction, not a bear market (Admirals analysis, a broker marketing piece)
Needs about 7.9% to regain the correction line

top.headline: US proposes new tariffs on 14 partners as hot inflation lifts December Fed hike odds
top.why: New Section 301 tariffs plus hotter PCE inflation and strong growth keep the hike case alive, the main threat to the equity rebound.
points: USTR proposed actions in 14 Section 301 excess-capacity probes on 25 November; not yet in force (Reuters, AP)
Core PCE for October came in at 3.3% y/y vs 3.2% forecast (Admirals citing BEA); Q3 GDP 4.3% per CME commentary
Admirals cites futures pricing a 25bp hike on 9 December as base case (as of 18 Nov); Waller argued for 50bp

top.headline: United draw 2-2 at Sporting as Lammens error and Tielemans red mar Pochettino's second game
top.why: Pochettino saw a better pressing display but the same sloppiness; the next test is his first home game with United second-bottom of the league.
points: Champions League draw in Lisbon on 25 Nov: two first-half penalties conceded, one saved.
Lammens spilled the ball for Sporting's equaliser; BBC reports Ashley Young saying he is one mistake from being dropped.
Tielemans was sent off in stoppage time after two bookings.
Pochettino: 'We've only been working together one week'; he wants more concentration.
top.next: Home to Brentford, Saturday 28 Nov, 3pm GMT (Brentford FC preview: United second-bottom, one point from safety, no league win since 30 Aug).

stories.headline: United, Liverpool and Spurs use same law firm to prepare damages claims against Man City
stories.why: A possible multi-hundred-million-pound claim linked to City's rule breaches; United say they lost prize money and commercial revenue from finishing second in 2012.
points: Guardian: the three clubs engaged Wiggin; Arsenal use HFS Kramer; claims would be separate.
Clubs lodged legal notices in November 2024 to avoid time-bar; activity stepped up after the Premier League's September finding against City.
City deny wrongdoing and have appealed; the Guardian says a new three-person panel hears it next month.
stories.next: City's appeal hearing in December (date not given in the source).

stories.headline: UK net migration falls to 77,000, lowest since 1997 outside the pandemic
stories.why: The sharpest drop on record in the post-pandemic series removes much of the immigration pressure from the UK political debate, though the estimate carries extra uncertainty. It also feeds into labour supply and population growth.
points: Provisional net migration was 77,000 in the year to June 2026, down from 204,000 a year earlier (revised)
Immigration fell 17% to 738,000; emigration was 661,000
Non-EU+ work-related arrivals fell 45,000, study 33,000 and asylum 19,000
UK population estimated at 69.6 million (+0.12%); British estimates rely on a 15-month projection and may be revised (update due May 2027)
stories.next: ONS update to British-national estimates, May 2027

stories.headline: Bank of England FPC warns AI financing and sovereign debt risks could crystallise together
stories.why: The UK financial stability regulator links higher yields, Middle East energy shocks and AI-funding volatility, supporting the higher-for-longer rate backdrop.
points: Record of the 19 November FPC meeting published 26 November
Gilt and other advanced-economy yields near two-decade highs, mainly on higher expected policy rates
AI financing described as increasingly complex, circular and opaque, raising contagion risk
Cyber and operational risks from AI agents flagged as more prominent

stories.headline: Anthropic says Claude wrote its Rust API rewrite in a week, with 70% less CPU
stories.why: A frontier lab reports migrating live production infrastructure with agents and no downtime; the lesson is that verification, not code-writing, is now the bottleneck. The performance figures are Anthropic's own.
points: Messages API moved from Python to Rust; Claude wrote the code in about a week, per InfoWorld's account of Anthropic's engineering post
Anthropic reports about 70% less CPU per request, 80% less memory and roughly 20% faster median time to first token
The production API was used as the verifier: it ran the Rust version on live traffic, flagged differences and dispatched agents to fix them
API traffic grew more than 1,800x from early 2024 to fall 2026, per Anthropic
stories.next: No dated catalyst; watch for independent engineers replicating the verify-on-production pattern.

stories.headline: Claude gains Skills over MCP in beta and a 10,000-plugin store
stories.why: If you build or use MCP connectors, servers can now ship workflow instructions alongside tools, so one update reaches every user. It is Anthropic's push to own the agent extension gateway.
points: Skills over MCP public beta announced 24 Nov; Claude Code needs version 2.1.331 or later
Skills load on demand and update server-side; Tasks and Elicitation moved to general availability the same day
BigGo reports Connectors and Skills merged into Plugins with a directory of 10,000+ plugins, open to Free, Pro, Max and Ultra, Team and Enterprise to follow
Removing a plugin does not automatically revoke its OAuth or token connection, so permissions need managing separately (BigGo)
stories.next: Team and Enterprise plugin rollout, no date given.

stories.headline: Claude Duet agent preview expands to Japan, India, Brazil and Indonesia
stories.why: Anthropic's always-on agent, which works while your devices are off, is going overseas a month after its US launch. It is a live test of autonomous inbox and calendar handling.
points: US research preview began 21 Oct as a waitlist; expansion announced 25 Nov, live in Japan from 26 Nov
Runs a dedicated browser on a virtual machine and patrols connected Gmail, Slack and calendars
Invitations going to Pro, Max and Ultra waitlist users; Team admins get a phased rollout
Reset credits during the preview expire 15 Dec; features may change at any time
stories.next: Credits expire 15 Dec; Team plan rollout undated.

stories.headline: KPMG launches cyber services on Claude Mythos for enterprise clients
stories.why: A Big Four firm is putting Anthropic's restricted cyber model into client work, an early sign of paid deployment of vulnerability-hunting AI.
points: KPMG LLP says it is part of Anthropic's Cyber Verification Programme
Four initial areas: codebase vulnerability scanning and attack chains, identity attack paths, breach pathway analysis, data-risk review
Deployed in clients' own secure environments
Quote from Anthropic Deputy CISO Jason Clinton in KPMG's announcement; no pricing given

stories.headline: Pinterest opens ad inventory to Microsoft Advertising campaigns
stories.why: Microsoft Ads buyers can reach Pinterest from their existing tools, which may add a cheap test channel for Q4 and 2027 shopping campaigns.
points: Eligible Microsoft Advertising campaigns can run in Pinterest Home Feed, Search Results and Related Pins via custom bidding
Launches first in North America, Australia and New Zealand
Pinterest cites 661 million monthly users and about 80 billion monthly searches, over half with commercial intent
Analyst commentary is Zacks; performance results not yet published
stories.next: No dated catalyst; watch for early placement reports in Microsoft Ads.

stories.headline: Church of England abuse Redress Scheme to open in January 2027, helpline from 7 December
stories.why: The CofE's long-promised compensation scheme for survivors of church-related abuse now has a start window, a test of the institution's response to the safeguarding failures behind it.
points: The scheme opens in January 2027; an independent Redress Helpline starts on 7 December.
It was first announced in 2020 after IICSA recommendations and other safeguarding reviews.
Redress includes acknowledgement, support and financial payments; an independent Appeal Authority has been appointed.
Lead safeguarding bishop Robert Springett wrote to parishes and cathedrals saying it 'cannot undo the harm'.
stories.next: Redress Helpline and application information go live 7 December 2026; scheme opens January 2027.

stories.headline: BMJ: ADHD medication in pregnancy not linked to autism or ADHD in children, 3.6m-child Nordic study
stories.why: Many women stop ADHD medication in pregnancy on thin evidence; this large registry study found no overall neurodevelopmental signal, supporting a shared decision with a clinician rather than automatic discontinuation.
points: Registers from Denmark, Norway and Sweden covered 3,643,376 children born 2000-2021, median follow-up about 9-10 years.
Exposure was rare (0.2% overall); methylphenidate was most common, then amphetamines (20%) and atomoxetine (7%).
No increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders overall; some raised risks for second/third-trimester exposure to specific drugs were seen and not fully explained.
Adjusted for sex, birth year, maternal age, education, smoking, ADHD diagnosis and other medication.
stories.next: Watch for clinical guidance responses and the detail on the trimester-specific signals; no dated catalyst.
stories.study: Population registry cohort, 3.6m children (Denmark, Norway, Sweden), maternal ADHD medication exposure; observational, residual confounding by indication possible, exposure rare. Details taken from secondary coverage; BMJ paper not read.

stories.headline: Semaglutide's SELECT benefits held across frailty levels, JAMA analysis
stories.why: Relevant to the GLP-1 threads: the cardiovascular benefit did not depend on baseline frailty, and frailty status itself improved more on the drug.
points: Primary cardiovascular risk rose with baseline frailty, but semaglutide's effect was broadly consistent across frailty categories.
It also reduced the heart-failure composite, all-cause hospitalisation and all-cause mortality across frailty levels.
By week 104, frailty improvement was more likely (OR 2.46, 95% CI 1.80-3.37) and worsening less likely (OR 0.47, 0.34-0.65) than placebo.
Quality-of-life gains appeared greater with higher baseline frailty.
stories.study: Post hoc analysis of the SELECT randomised trial (adults with obesity and established cardiovascular disease); secondary, not powered for frailty subgroups; Novo-funded trial. Read via trade summary only.

stories.headline: GTA VI doubles UK games retail to £142m in launch week, NielsenIQ says
stories.why: Independent retail data confirms GTA VI's pull on hardware as well as software, with PS5 and Xbox console sales jumping in launch week.
points: NIQ, 19-21 Nov: UK games retail revenue £142m; GTA VI physical sales £32m, 74% of physical software; PS5 hardware +46% week-on-week, Xbox Series X|S +75%.
AppMagic via GamesIndustry.biz: over 39m unique players on PlayStation, 683m hours, 17.4 hours average.
GTA VI was the first game played on 70% of new PS5 consoles.
stories.next: Panini GTA VI trading cards due in December 2026 (per Panini statement via ScreenRant).

stories.headline: More PS5 owners report sudden shutdowns playing GTA VI; cause unproven
stories.why: If you play GTA VI on a PS5, heat or ageing hardware may be the issue rather than the game; no Sony or Rockstar response yet.
points: A console repair technician on X reports more PS5s arriving with sudden shutdowns during GTA VI.
Logs showed Main SoC Access, APU VRM Power Fail and SSD Controller Watchdog errors.
GAMINGbible says the game is unlikely the sole culprit and had no reply from Rockstar or Sony.
One console in the report had 235 days of runtime.
stories.next: Rockstar or Sony comment, or patch notes (no date).

stories.headline: GTA VI PS5 dump reportedly runs on jailbroken console as PC emulation work continues
stories.why: Piracy and PC-port attempts are widening beyond the Xbox build leak, adding pressure on Take-Two; there is still no official PC version.
points: Notebookcheck: videos on 25 Nov show a PS5 game dump running on firmware 11.60 via a jailbreak; retail needs 14.23.
Reported 540 GB files circulating on piracy networks; the KytyPS5 emulator is a possible PC route, with performance far off.
Take-Two has shut Discord servers and issued DMCA takedowns on GitHub repositories after the Cyberleek Xbox build.
Shattered.io: Rockstar has announced no PC version; Q1 2027 PC talk is unconfirmed.
stories.next: Further Take-Two takedowns or any Rockstar PC announcement (no date).

stories.headline: Nature reports dual AI and human proofs of the Riemann hypothesis, awaiting checking
stories.why: If either holds, it settles the best-known open problem about prime numbers and would be a landmark for AI in mathematics; the claims are not yet verified.
points: Nature News (25 Nov) says two proofs, one AI-written and one human-written, have stunned mathematicians; experts say both need careful checking.
The hypothesis dates from Riemann's 1859 paper and concerns how far prime counts stray from the expected pattern, roughly a square-root error term.
Nature also ran an explainer likening it to a familiar statistical margin-of-error test.
Detail on authors and method was not in the saved text, so treat as unverified.
stories.next: Expert checking of both proofs; no dated catalyst.
